stem: How many of the athletes who completed the study were swimmers or rowers?
stimulus:
A sports science lab enrolled 240 athletes in a 12-week study of recovery after training. By the end of the study, 180 athletes had completed it. The table shows how the athletes who completed the study were split by primary sport, as a percentage of the 180 who completed it.

Athletes Who Completed the Study, by Primary Sport
Primary sport | Percent of completers
Track | 40%
Swimming | 15%
Rowing | 20%
Cycling | 25%
explanation: The question asks about swimmers or rowers, so first add the two percentages: 15% + 20% = 35%. The table's percentages are out of the 180 athletes who completed the study, not the 240 who enrolled. So $0.35 \times 180 = 63$.

A.why: You found only the rowers, $0.20 \times 180 = 36$, and left out the swimmers. The question asks for swimmers or rowers, so you need to add the two percentages before you multiply.

C.why: You took 35% of the 240 athletes who enrolled, which gives $0.35 \times 240 = 84$. The table gives percentages of the 180 athletes who completed the study, so 180 is the total to use.

D.why: You found the athletes who were neither swimmers nor rowers, $0.65 \times 180 = 117$. The question asks for the athletes who were swimmers or rowers, which is the other 35%.

stem: How many parcels in the district are designated for affordable housing?
stimulus: An urban planning office surveyed a district that has 3,600 land parcels. Of these parcels, 40% are zoned residential. Of the residential parcels, 15% are designated for affordable housing. No parcel outside the residential zone carries this designation.
explanation: First find the residential parcels: $0.40 \times 3{,}600 = 1{,}440$. The 15% applies only to those residential parcels, so $0.15 \times 1{,}440 = 216$ parcels are designated for affordable housing.

B.why: You took 15% of all 3,600 parcels, $0.15 \times 3{,}600 = 540$. The 15% is a percentage of the residential parcels only, so you have to find the residential count first.

C.why: You found the residential parcels that are not designated for affordable housing, $0.85 \times 1{,}440 = 1{,}224$. The question asks for the 15% that are designated.

D.why: 1,440 is the number of residential parcels, $0.40 \times 3{,}600$. That is only the first step. You still need to take 15% of it.

stem: How many of the seeds germinated and were not culled?
stimulus: In an agricultural science trial, researchers planted 1,200 seeds of a drought-tolerant sorghum variety. Of the seeds planted, 85% germinated. Of the seeds that germinated, 20% produced seedlings that were later culled for weak root growth.
explanation: First find the seeds that germinated: $0.85 \times 1{,}200 = 1{,}020$. The 20% that were culled is 20% of the germinated seeds, so 80% of them were kept: $0.80 \times 1{,}020 = 816$.

A.why: You found the germinated seeds that were culled, $0.20 \times 1{,}020 = 204$. The question asks for the seeds that were not culled, which is the other 80%.

B.why: You subtracted the percentages, 85% − 20% = 65%, and took 65% of 1,200. The 20% is out of the 1,020 germinated seeds, not out of all 1,200, so you can't subtract it from 85%. You have to multiply in two steps.

D.why: 1,020 is the number of seeds that germinated. You stopped before removing the culled seedlings.

stem: How many samplers in the collection are in neither the silk-on-linen category nor the wool-on-linen category?
stimulus:
A textile history museum catalogued its 520 surviving eighteenth-century needlework samplers by thread and ground fabric. Each sampler is in exactly one category.

Samplers in the Collection, by Thread and Ground Fabric
Category | Percent of samplers
Silk on linen | 45%
Wool on linen | 30%
Silk on wool | 15%
Other | 10%
explanation: The samplers in neither of the two named categories are the silk-on-wool and the other samplers: 15% + 10% = 25%. Each sampler is in exactly one category, so you can also get this as 100% − 45% − 30%. Then $0.25 \times 520 = 130$.

A.why: You found only the samplers in the other category, $0.10 \times 520 = 52$. You left out the silk-on-wool samplers, which are also in neither named category.

B.why: You found only the silk-on-wool samplers, $0.15 \times 520 = 78$. You left out the samplers in the other category, which are also in neither named category.

D.why: You added the two named categories, 45% + 30% = 75%, and found $0.75 \times 520 = 390$. That counts the samplers in either category. The question asks for the samplers in neither.

stem: How many millimeters of rainfall did the station record in June of that year?
stimulus: A meteorology station's 30-year average rainfall for June is 85 millimeters. In one unusually wet year, the station recorded June rainfall equal to 160% of that 30-year average.
explanation: 160% of 85 means $1.60 \times 85 = 136$. The station recorded 136 millimeters of rainfall in June.

A.why: You found $0.60 \times 85 = 51$. That is how much the June rainfall was above the average, not the total rainfall.

C.why: You added the 60 from the percentage to 85 as if it were 60 millimeters. A 60% increase on 85 is $0.60 \times 85 = 51$ millimeters, not 60.

D.why: You read "160% of the average" as "160% more than the average" and found $85 + 1.60 \times 85 = 221$. "Of" means multiply, so the rainfall is $1.60 \times 85$.

stem: How many of the 640 fragments were identified as either linen or silk?
stimulus:
A textile museum received 640 cloth fragments from the site of an 18th-century weaving mill. Conservators were able to identify the fiber in 75% of the fragments. The table shows how the identified fragments were distributed by fiber.

Identified Fragments by Fiber
Fiber | Percent of identified fragments
Wool | 40%
Linen | 25%
Silk | 20%
Cotton | 15%
explanation: First find how many fragments had their fiber identified: $0.75 \times 640 = 480$. The table's percents are percents of these 480 fragments, not of all 640. Linen or silk is $25\% + 20\% = 45\%$ of the identified fragments, so the count is $0.45 \times 480 = 216$.

A.why: You found 25% of 480, which counts only the linen fragments. The question asks for linen or silk, so you need to add the two percents before you multiply.

C.why: You found 55% of 480, which counts the wool and cotton fragments. That is the part that is neither linen nor silk, the opposite of what the question asks.

D.why: You took 45% of all 640 fragments. The table gives percents of the identified fragments only, so you have to find 75% of 640 first and then take 45% of that.
